ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher of $4.33 (mileage refund for the unexempted 09:24–09:30 segment) under NS-7; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (no account flag on these facts)
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI journey (Raffles Place → Changi T3), so distance is directly chargeable and any unexplained extra kilometre is refundable mileage [F6][RD-2]. The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 09:24–09:30, in which 3.78 km was driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, adding 3.07 km and straying up to 688 m off the route; the trip overall ran 24.4 km against 21.2 km optimal [F3][F1][RD-1]. That segment is therefore unexempted unless a clause excuses it.

No exemption applies. RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the detour; the trace marks this ✗ and the record confirms no incident near the route in the trip window, with the only congestion records at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on ECP and Airport Boulevard — not bands 1–2 and, per RD-4(b), corroborative at most [F13][F11][F12][F14][RD-4]. RD-3 does not apply: the rider's only pre-segment message named the pickup point (Raffles Place taxi stand), and no stop was measured in the segment [F7][F8][RD-3]. On RD-5, the chat record is complete and fully timestamped with only two messages, both about the meeting point; no rider message before 09:24:50 proposes, names or approves any route, and the driver's post-trip statement that he "went where the GPS sent me" is not rider consent [F9][F7][F8][F10][RD-5]. With no rider agreement, the ground is consent_after_or_none and the segment counts — which is exactly the finding both advocates stipulated [F3][RD-5].

The refund follows the RD-2 formula: the fare record gives the trip's per-km rate as distance fare ÷ distance km, $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.4101/km; 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290 → $4.33 [F4][F6][F3][RD-2]. The billed excess-distance line of $4.51 covers 3.20 km; the residual ~0.13 km is route-corridor/map-matching movement not attributed to any segment, which RD-2 expressly leaves with the rider [F4][F3][RD-2]. Time units ($9.58 for 36.8 min), platform fee $1.47 and waiting $0.00 are not mileage units and are outside RD-2, and there is no additional add-on item in dispute (no surge, no destination-change charge) [F6][F5][FARE-1]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute but 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so the "repeated route breach" condition is not met and no account flag is warranted [F16][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The complete, timestamped chat contains only the rider's pickup note (09:04) and the driver's car note (09:05) before the 09:24 segment; no rider message proposes, names or approves any route or stop, and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted is not rider consent [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. No traffic incident corroborates reasonable cause and no rider-named stop exists [F13][RD-4][RD-3], so the segment's 3.07 extra km are refundable under RD-1/RD-2 [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that moderate 40–49 km/h flow across the expressway and airport approach could be a reasonable-cause ground fails: RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident (Accident/Roadwork/etc.) on the replaced optimal stretch, and F13 records none near the route in the trip window, while F11/F12 show only speed band 5, which under RD-4(b) corroborates at most and does not exempt [F13][F11][F12][RD-4]; the segment is therefore processed under RD-4(c) and RD-2 [F3][RD-2].

The submission that the absence of any rider route instruction means the driver was free to stray 688 m off the optimal route is rejected: RD-1 imposes on the driver the duty to take the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and the absence of rider consent removes the RD-5 exemption rather than creating one [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-1][RD-5].

The submission that no account action is available is rejected as framed, but the outcome is the same: the present unexempted route segment under RD-1 is recorded against the driver, yet RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 and F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account is issued [F16][F3][RD-6].

The request for a repeat-breach account review is rejected: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the 90-day window, and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes (2 disputes, 1 upheld, route: 0), so the flag condition is not met [F16][F15][RD-6].

The rider's own figure of $4.33 is correct, but any claim to more than that (the full $4.51 billed for 3.20 km) is rejected: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, and the residual 0.13 km of route-corridor/map-matching movement is not refundable [F4][F3][F6][RD-2].

Accepted only so far as it goes: F6 shows waiting $0.00, no destination-change charge and platform fee $1.47 with surge 1.0× [F6][F5], so no additional FARE-1 item exists; the disputed amount is confined to the distance figure [FARE-1].

what_would_change: F3: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $4.33 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.
